recognize_zh: 骨髓切片骨小樑旁的纖維間質中（圓圈）可見一群卵圓形寄生蟲卵，具有折光性的厚卵殼，內含嗜鹼性顆粒狀的毛蚴（miracidium），周圍少量發炎反應，符合血吸蟲卵（Schistosoma eggs）。
features: Low power (A): bone trabecula with adjacent fibrous marrow stroma containing a focal cluster of ova (circled)
High power (B): four to five oval eggs, roughly 100-150 µm long, each with a thin, refractile, eosinophilic shell
Egg contents with basophilic granular/cellular material consistent with developing miracidia
Surrounding fibrous stroma with scattered spindle cells and minimal inflammation; no well-formed granuloma or calcification visible in this field
A lateral or terminal spine is not clearly identified in these sections
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy (H&E) shows a bone trabecula with adjacent fibrotic, hypocellular stroma in which a cluster of parasitic ova is present (panel A). At higher magnification (panel B), the ova are oval with thin refractile eosinophilic shells enclosing basophilic granular miracidia, surrounded by fibrous tissue with only a mild inflammatory reaction. A diagnostic spine is not appreciated in this plane of section, so species assignment is not possible on morphology alone. Findings are consistent with schistosomal eggs deposited in the bone marrow; correlation with travel history, serology, and stool/urine examination is recommended.

ddx.vs: Paragonimus eggs are operculated with a thickened abopercular shell and are brown, whereas schistosome eggs lack an operculum and carry a lateral or terminal spine.
Coccidioides spherules are thick-walled round structures filled with small uniform endospores, not oval eggs containing a multicellular miracidium.
Fungal sporangia are round with numerous small spores and are GMS/PAS positive, lacking the ciliated larval structure of a miracidium.
Degenerated debris lacks a uniform oval shell with internal nucleated larval content and does not occur as a cluster of identical ova.
